haiku-low.q1: Keys load at start-up, before readiness. /healthz returns 200 only after all three keys have loaded.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. The pod stays not ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes it re-reads the store. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value and logs a warning.
haiku-low.q4: Values are held in memory only. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs.
haiku-low.q5: The orders-api-prod identity has read-only access to prod secrets. Only security on-call can write them. Engineers cannot read prod values.
haiku-low.q6: Keys are still in git history and copied into existing images. Old values become harmless only after rotation at the provider and revocation (step 9).
haiku-low.q7: Provider clients call secrets.get(name) on each use instead of copying the key at construction, so refreshed keys are seen.
haiku-low.q8: After the new version is written and the 5-minute refresh runs, every instance must report the new version id. Only then is the old key revoked.
haiku-low.q9: Set store access, copy keys into the store, switch the app to the store, remove keys from the committed file, then rotate at providers (after the deploy is verified).
haiku-low.q10: From the dev store orders-api/dev/* via make run (APP_ENV=dev), using the developer's dev access only.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided on scheduled rotation, and no cadence is set in the plan.

sonnet.q1: Keys load at start-up (load() reads all three); /healthz returns 200 (ready) only after all three keys have loaded.
sonnet.q2: load() retries 3 times, 2 s apart, then the process exits non-zero; the pod never becomes ready, the rollout halts, and old pods keep serving, so no customer impact.
sonnet.q3: refresh() re-reads the keys every 5 minutes. If it fails, the instance keeps the last good value and logs a warning.
sonnet.q4: Held in memory only. They must never appear on disk, in environment variables, or in logs.
sonnet.q5: Read: the prod identity orders-api-prod (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Engineers cannot read prod values. Write: only security on-call.
sonnet.q6: The file is committed to git and copied into every image, so old keys remain in git history/old images (implied by the doc: pre-migration images have old keys baked in). Rotating the keys at the providers and revoking the old ones makes them harmless, but only after all instances use the new keys.
sonnet.q7: Provider clients (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) call secrets.get(name) on each use rather than copying the key at construction, so they see the refreshed value.
sonnet.q8: After the 5-minute refresh wait, check that every instance reports the new version id (via secret_versions on /healthz). Only then revoke the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set access rules, 2) copy keys into the store, 3-5) add loader, switch clients, readiness, 6) remove keys from repo, 7) local runs to dev, 8) deploy and verify, 9) rotate then revoke. So: access, copy, switch app, remove from file, rotate. (Step 6 is listed before deploy in the doc; the doc does not explicitly state ordering beyond step 2 starting after step 1 and step 9 after step 8.)
sonnet.q10: From the dev store, orders-api/dev/* (sandbox keys), because make run sets APP_ENV=dev. Developers have dev access only, never prod. Which identity make run uses is NOT STATED beyond developers' dev access.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Rotation cadence is an open question that security has not decided; no cadence is set.
